note: Entity Type Clone is two forms and a batch worker: entity_type_clone.type (/admin/config/entity-type-clone, the module's configure route) clones a bundle plus its FieldConfigs and its enabled form/view displays, and entity_type_clone.role (/admin/config/role-clone) creates a new user_role and calls user_role_grant_permissions() with the source role's permissions. Both routes require the single permission 'access entity type clone', which also gates the 'Clone X' entity operation added to node/paragraph/taxonomy_term/profile bundle listings. Clonable entity types are block_content, node and taxonomy_term always, plus paragraph/profile/storage when those modules exist. The module has no config, no schema, no services, no Drush commands and no plugin types. Medium cases read live role permissions and live bundle/field configuration; hard cases require actually producing the cloned bundle (type + field + both displays) and the cloned role (identical permission set) on the running site.

evals.prompt: The entity_type_clone module is installed on a Drupal 11 site. What are the two admin paths it adds, and which permission does a user need to use them?
evals.expected_output: It adds /admin/config/entity-type-clone (route entity_type_clone.type, the module's configure route, for cloning bundles) and /admin/config/role-clone (route entity_type_clone.role, for cloning user roles). Both require the permission 'access entity type clone', which also controls the 'Clone <label>' operation link added to the content type, vocabulary, paragraph type and profile type listings.

evals.prompt: Which entity types can Drupal's entity_type_clone module clone bundles for, and what does the clone actually copy across besides the bundle itself?
evals.expected_output: Always block_content, node and taxonomy_term; plus paragraph, profile and storage when the paragraphs, profile or storage modules are enabled. The batch copies the bundle entity itself, every bundle-level FieldConfig (base fields and taxonomy's 'parent' are skipped, and fields already present on the target are skipped), every enabled form-mode and view-mode display, third-party view-display settings such as field_group, and the source's extra-field visibility. Field storage is shared, not duplicated, and no content is cloned.

evals.prompt: How does the role cloning feature of Drupal's entity_type_clone module work - what exactly ends up on the new role, and what is not copied?
evals.expected_output: The CloneRole form at /admin/config/role-clone creates a new user_role entity from the label and machine name you type, then calls user_role_grant_permissions($new_id, $source_role->getPermissions()), so the clone gets exactly the source role's permission list. Nothing else is copied - not the weight, not is_admin, and no users are assigned to the new role.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there are two roles whose machine names start with etc_probe_. Inspect the running site and tell me which one of them is allowed to use the Entity Type Clone admin forms, and name the permission that decides it.
evals.expected_output: etc_probe_beta. It holds the permission 'access entity type clone' (the requirement on both entity_type_clone.type and entity_type_clone.role); etc_probe_alpha only has 'access content'.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has a content type etc_known_src plus two candidates, etc_known_a and etc_known_b. Only one of them is a complete Entity Type Clone of etc_known_src - that is, it carries every field that etc_known_src has. Inspect the live field configuration and tell me which one, and which field the other one is missing.
evals.expected_output: etc_known_b is the complete clone: like etc_known_src it has both field_etc_known and field_etc_extra. etc_known_a only has field_etc_known and is missing field_etc_extra.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site has the entity_type_clone module installed. The content type etc_task_src ('ETC Task Source') has a field field_etc_task that is configured on its default form display and its default view display. Produce a clone of that content type with the machine name etc_task_dst and the label 'ETC Task Destination', including the field and both displays, and apply it to the live site.
evals.expected_output: A node_type etc_task_dst must exist, a FieldConfig node.etc_task_dst.field_etc_task must exist, and field_etc_task must be a component of both core.entity_form_display.node.etc_task_dst.default and core.entity_view_display.node.etc_task_dst.default - the end state produced by the Entity Type Clone batch (CloneEntityType::cloneEntityTypeData plus cloneEntityTypeField).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there is a user role called 'ETC Role Source' (machine name etc_role_src). I need a second role that can do exactly the same things, called 'ETC Role Destination' with the machine name etc_role_dst. Please set that up on the live site.
evals.expected_output: A user_role etc_role_dst must exist whose permission list is identical to etc_role_src's ('access content', 'access user profiles', 'view own unpublished content') - the result of entity_type_clone's CloneRole form, i.e. Role::create() followed by user_role_grant_permissions() with the source role's permissions.
